root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before caching `_table_data.toc = {_storage.data() + toffset()};`, the APFS B-tree constructor must require the TOC offset to stay inside the current node buffer: `(obj_type() == APFS_OBJ_TYPE_BTREE_NODE || obj_type() == APFS_OBJ_TYPE_BTREE_ROOTNODE) && toffset() <= _storage.size()`. The vulnerable original only admits the node by object type and then caches an out-of-block TOC pointer; the fixed source adds the missing TOC bounds guard at this exact line.
root_cause_criterion.description: The sanitizer trace points to `key()` reading through `_table_data.toc.fixed[0]`, and Stage 02 traced that pointer back to `_storage.data() + toffset()` in the constructor. The missing root obligation is the TOC bound check `toffset() <= _storage.size()` before `_table_data.toc` may be cached.

nodes.state: At `const auto &t = _table_data.toc.fixed[index];`, the cached TOC base pointer still lies beyond `_storage.data() + _storage.size()`, so loading `t.key_offset` performs the AddressSanitizer-reported out-of-block read.

edges.relation: The constructor stores `_storage.data() + toffset()` into `_table_data.toc`, and `key()` later reads through that same cached pointer as `_table_data.toc.fixed[index]`.
